definitions.explanation: The seven bright stars of Ursa Major that form a ladle shape, widely used as a guide for finding the North Star.

examples.japanese: {北斗|ほくと}{七星|しちせい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: I can see the Big Dipper.

examples.japanese: {北斗|ほくと}{七星|しちせい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{北極星|ほっきょくせい}→北極星：30629_hokkyokusei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}した→探す：00493_sagasu⟧。
examples.english: I used the Big Dipper to find the North Star.

examples.japanese: ⟦{空気|くうき}→空気：01390_kuuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{澄|す}んだ→澄む：13370_sumu⟧⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{北斗|ほくと}{七星|しちせい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦はっきり→はっきり：01228_hakkiri⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: On a clear winter night, the Big Dipper is clearly visible.

notes:
Composed of {北斗|ほくと} (the Northern Dipper) + {七星|しちせい} (seven stars). The seven stars form the well-known ladle shape within the constellation {大熊座|おおぐまざ} (Ursa Major).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {北斗|ほくと}{七星|しちせい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つける→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧: to spot the Big Dipper
- {北斗|ほくと}{七星|しちせい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧: the shape of the Big Dipper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{北極星|ほっきょくせい}→北極星：30629_hokkyokusei⟧: the North Star — found by following the Dipper's two end stars
- ⟦{南十字星|みなみじゅうじせい}→南十字星：29540_minamijuujisei⟧: the Southern Cross — its southern-sky counterpart
